intro.title: Accessibility (a11y) Fundamentals
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React form with accessible labels, error messages, and focus management to ensure it's usable by everyone, including people with disabilities. You'll learn core accessibility concepts like semantic HTML, ARIA attributes, and keyboard navigation. The main technologies involved are React components, JSX, and built-in HTML accessibility features. By the end, you'll understand how to make web applications more inclusive and compliant with accessibility standards.
intro.usecase: Accessibility (a11y) fundamentals are essential in any real-world React application that serves diverse users, including those with disabilities. For example, in e-commerce sites, accessible forms ensure screen readers can announce input labels and error messages during checkout, while accessible navigation menus allow keyboard users to browse product categories. Developers implement these a11y patterns in dashboards with proper ARIA roles for data tables, modals that trap focus for user interactions, and interactive filters with clear announcements for dynamic content updates, ensuring compliance and inclusive user experiences.
